gui.how-to-circle.title: How to Circle
gui.how-to-circle.mode.tooltip: Circle uses one diameter (height follows width). Oval uses separate width and height.
gui.how-to-circle.fill.tooltip: Filled shows every block from the centre to the edge. Outline shows only the perimeter.
gui.how-to-circle.centre.tooltip: Auto: odd sizes get a 1-block centre, even sizes a 2-block centre. Forcing 1×1 or 2×2 changes the size by one block so the shape stays exactly centred (shown in yellow).
gui.how-to-circle.align.tooltip: Even sizes are centred on a block corner, so the centre is 2 blocks wide. This picks which neighbour of the selected block forms the rest of the centre. Mixed sizes (e.g. 21×12) have a 1×2 centre.
gui.how-to-circle.generate.tooltip: Show the hologram at the selected centre (or at your position if no centre was selected yet).
gui.how-to-circle.label_format.tooltip: Long by short: a 1-wide, 5-long column reads "5 by 1". Width by height: it reads "1 by 5".
gui.how-to-circle.select_centre.tooltip: Look at a block and left-click to place the centre (right-click to cancel). The centre goes on the face you look at; sneak to use the block itself.
gui.how-to-circle.lock_centre.tooltip: ON: the centre is the block you stand in. OFF: for even sizes, the centre snaps to the block corner nearest your exact position.
gui.how-to-circle.offset.tooltip: Vertical offset in blocks. Click to reset.
gui.how-to-circle.reset_position.tooltip: Reset offset, rotation, plane and alignment, and re-centre on your position.
gui.how-to-circle.see_through.tooltip: Draw the hologram on top of terrain, e.g. to plan underground or inside a build.
gui.how-to-circle.info.invalid: Enter a whole number from 1 to %s
hud.how-to-circle.selecting: How to Circle — select the centre
hud.how-to-circle.help: Left-click: confirm · Right-click or J: cancel · Sneak: use block itself
message.how-to-circle.selecting: Centre selection: look at a block and left-click. Right-click to cancel.
message.how-to-circle.no_target: No block targeted — look at a block to set the centre.
